title: Run post-SBP reality check and smart goal
description:
After the SBP visibility/MCP recalibration bead is closed, run a repo-vs-vision reality check followed by a `$smart goal` pass from this repo root.

Prompt to run:
`$reality-check-for-project + $smart goal`

The point is not a brainstorm. Compare implemented code, docs, plans, Beads, and validation commands against the project vision; then write the single most accretive smart-goal contract for the next move. If the pass discovers truly accretive follow-up work, create/update Beads with evidence and dependencies.
design:
concern: post-visibility project truth and next smart goal
writes: Beads issue notes/children and overlay-backed smart-chain artifacts if the repo has a matching invocation root
non_goals: broad brainstorm; implementation before the reality check names the next move
validation: repo-native validation named by the smart goal, plus Beads dependency/state check
acceptance_criteria:
- The SBP recalibration bead is closed or its unresolved blocker is explicitly accepted as not blocking this repo assessment.
- `$reality-check-for-project + $smart goal` was run from the repo root with repo evidence, not vibes.
- The reality check distinguishes implemented state from roadmap/planned state.
- The smart goal names loop_goal, success criteria, resume condition, and validation/commit/reality-check gate.
- Any new follow-up Beads are evidence-backed, dependency-linked, and not duplicates.
- Repo-native validation commands are named or exact blockers are recorded.
notes: Backlog refresh 2026-05-11T23:06:37.806447+00:00: confirmed this repo should have this operational bead.

title: Run SBP skill and MCP visibility recalibration
description:
Run a repo-local `$sbp` recalibration from this repo root before more agent work relies on skill or MCP visibility.

Required read-only pass:
- `sbp`
- `sbp recalibrate`
- `sbp skills --issues-only --no-global --format json`
- `sbp mcp --format json`
- `sbp beads status`

Classify any `missing_for_cwd`, `scope_violations`, `broken_project`, MCP missing/extra/parity drift, and Beads drift. Use narrow dry-runs before applying any sync/remove/prune action. Prefer repo-local fixes; do not do broad global cleanup unless the evidence is specific and recorded here.
design:
concern: Skillbox visibility and MCP parity
writes: project-local skill links, `.mcp.json`, `.codex/config.toml`, repo-local Beads notes only when justified by dry-run evidence
non_goals: broad global pruning; making task skills global to unblock a single run
validation: sbp recalibrate; sbp mcp --format json; sbp beads status
acceptance_criteria:
- SBP read-only commands above were run from the repo root and summarized in issue notes.
- Add/remove/sync decisions are classified by mismatch type and policy reason.
- Any mutation used a reviewed dry-run first, then the narrow apply command only.
- `sbp recalibrate` and `sbp mcp --format json` were rerun after changes, or exact blockers were recorded.
- Remaining human decisions, if any, are explicit.
notes: Backlog refresh 2026-05-11T23:06:37.717811+00:00: confirmed this repo should have this operational bead.

title: Harden Cargo package hygiene before next feature work
description: Recommendation: before adding new parser or emit features, make the crate package boundary explicit and reconcile release docs that drifted after v0.2.0 shipped.
design:
repo_state:
  repo_head: 7856897 (v0.2.0)
  compared_to: none; first beads-backed smart link
repo_signals:
  - git describe reports v0.2.0 and git tag lists v0.2.0, but CHANGELOG.md still says 0.2.0 is prepared, not tagged
  - AGENTS.md names .github/workflows/release.yml, then later says no CI config was found
  - cargo package --locked --list was blocked by newly initialized beads dirty state
  - cargo package --locked --list --allow-dirty includes .beads/ and .buildooor/ overlay files because Cargo.toml does not exclude them
  - cargo test --locked, cargo fmt -- --check, and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed
integrity_gap:
  package and release metadata boundaries are not explicit enough for a published crate with repo-local beads and overlay state
hardening_decision:
  hardening-first; build/test code is green, but packaging and release docs can leak or mislead before the next publish
loop_goal:
  make the next clawgs release/package boundary boring, private-state-free, and accurately documented
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria:
- Cargo.toml explicitly excludes .beads/, .buildooor/, backup files, .env files, and equivalent repo-local operator state from crates.io packages.
- .github/workflows/release.yml fails if package contents include .beads/, .buildooor/, backup files, .env files, or overlay state.
- CHANGELOG.md correctly reflects that v0.2.0 is tagged/shipped in this checkout, not merely prepared.
- AGENTS.md no longer contradicts itself about CI/release workflow presence.
- README schema links are absolute GitHub URLs for crates.io rendering.
- cargo fmt -- --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked, and cargo package --locked --list --allow-dirty pass with clean package contents.
notes:
chain_context:
  first beads-backed smart link; no prior chain:smart issue; no modes report found under the resolved evaluation root
modes:
  report: none found
  takeaway: none
crap_status:
  not run in this pass; prior git history claims CRAP hotspot reduction, and current cargo test/fmt/clippy are green
first_step:
  patch Cargo.toml exclude plus release workflow package checks to reject .beads/, .buildooor/, AGENTS.md.bak, backup files, and local overlay state; update CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, and README release/link wording
resume_condition:
  complete; rerun /smart after this package hygiene patch is committed or if the next release/package gate finds new drift
validation:
  cargo fmt -- --check passed
  cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed
  cargo test --locked passed
  cargo package --locked --list --allow-dirty passed forbidden-path scan with 32 package files
  Cargo.toml.orig is Cargo-generated and expected in package archives, so it is not a forbidden package path
